q: The two main classes of nucleic acids are deoxyribonucleic acid and ____ acid. (2025- Set 11)
e: The two main classes of nucleic acids are deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) and ribonucleic acid (RNA).

q: Hydrogen bonds link each complementary ____ pair. (2026- Set 2)
e: Hydrogen bonds link each complementary base pair in the DNA molecule.

q: The two strands of a DNA molecule are ____. (2025- Set 12 / 2026- Set 1)
e: The two strands of a DNA molecule run in opposite directions and are antiparallel.

q: DNA is a double helix structure consisting of two ____ strands twine around each other. (2025- Set 8)
e: DNA consists of two polynucleotide strands twined around each other to form a double helix.

q: Each polynucleotide strand is made up of many ____ molecules. (2025- Set 5 / 2026- နိုင်ငံခြား)
e: Each polynucleotide strand is composed of repeating nucleotide units.

q: The pyrimidine bases have a ____ ring in their chemical structure. (2025- Set 10)
e: Pyrimidines have a single six-membered ring structure.

q: Hydrogen bonds link each complementary ____ pair in DNA. (2025- Set 1)
e: Complementary base pairs in DNA are held together by hydrogen bonds.

q: Hydrogen bonds link each ____ base pair. (2025- Set 2)
e: Hydrogen bonds specifically hold complementary base pairs together in DNA.

q: Each DNA strand forms a backbone of alternating ____ groups and sugars. (2024-Set 3/2025-Set 1)
e: The backbone of a DNA strand consists of alternating sugar and phosphate groups.

q: Hydrogen bonds link each complementary ____ pair. (2024-နိုင်ငံခြား)
e: Hydrogen bonds join complementary base pairs together.

q: Only three different RNA molecules involved in ____ synthesis. (2025- Set 3)
e: Three main types of RNA (mRNA, tRNA, rRNA) participate in protein synthesis.

q: DNA is the hereditary material responsible for passing genetic ____ from cell to cell and generation to generation. (2024-Set 4)
e: DNA carries the genetic information required for inheritance across cells and generations.

q: In total, there are around 3.2 billion base pairs in the DNA of a typical ____ cell. (2025- Set 13)
e: A typical mammalian cell contains approximately 3.2 billion base pairs of DNA.

q: DNA replication is made by a ____ method. (2025- Set 3)
e: DNA replication follows a semiconservative model where each new double strand retains one original strand.

q: Proteins and enzymes assist in ____ of DNA. (2025- Set 4)
e: Various proteins and enzymes work together to carry out DNA replication.

q: Each time the DNA replicates, some ____ from the chromosome are lost. (2025- Set 7)
e: With each round of replication, small amounts of nucleotides at chromosome ends are lost.

q: DNA ____ is the making of an exact copy of the DNA molecule. (2024-Set 4)
e: DNA replication produces an exact duplicate of a DNA molecule.

q: Proteins and ____ assist in replication of DNA. (2024-နောက်ဆက်တွဲမေးခွန်း)
e: Enzymes and specialized proteins drive the processes of DNA replication.

q: More than one codon can code for the same amino acid is called ____. (2025- Set 6)
e: The genetic code is redundant because multiple codons can specify the same amino acid.

q: The translation of ____ sequence to amino acid sequence uses the genetic code. (2025- Set 6)
e: Translation converts the nucleotide sequence of mRNA into an amino acid sequence.

q: The two steps in protein synthesis are ____ and translation. (2024-ရန်ကုန်နှင့်တိုင်းခရိုင်အချို့စုစည်းမေး)
e: Protein synthesis consists of two main stages: transcription and translation.

q: The two steps in ____ synthesis are transcription and translation. (2024-Set 3)
e: Protein synthesis includes transcription followed by translation.

q: Transcription occurs in the ____ of the cell. (2024-ရန်ကုန်နှင့်တိုင်းခရိုင်အချို့စုစည်းမေး)(2025- Set 12)
e: In eukaryotic cells, transcription takes place inside the nucleus.

q: Transgenic bacteria, plants and animals are commonly referred to as ____ modified organisms. (2025- Set 8, 11)
e: Genetically modified organisms (GMOs) include transgenic bacteria, plants, and animals.

q: Golden rice contains a lot of the ____ pigment beta-carotene. (2025- Set 4 / 2026-နိုင်ငံခြား)
e: Golden rice is engineered to produce beta-carotene, an orange pigment.

q: Golden Rice contains a lot of the orange ____ beta-carotene. (2025- Set 9)
e: Beta-carotene is an orange pigment found in enriched golden rice.

q: Genetic engineering crops are increased heat and ____ tolerance. (2025- Set 2)
e: Genetically engineered crops often have improved tolerance to environmental stresses like drought and heat.

q: One type of antibody made by corn can deliver radioisotopes to ____ cells. (2025- Set 5, 10)
e: Corn-produced antibodies can specifically target tumour cells to deliver therapeutic radioisotopes.

q: Vitamin A deficiency can cause ____. (2025- Set 13)
e: Vitamin A deficiency is a leading cause of preventable blindness.

q: Rice is a ____ food in many parts of the world. (2024-Set 2)
e: Rice serves as a primary staple food for a large portion of the global population.

q: The milk of female transgenic offspring contains human growth ____. (2025- Set 9)
e: Transgenic animals can be produced to express human growth protein in their milk.

q: The milk of female transgenic offspring contains ____ growth protein. (2024-နိုင်ငံခြား / 2026- Set 1)
e: Transgenic livestock can produce human growth protein in their milk.

q: Benefits of GM animals are increased higher ____ yield in cows. (2024-Set 2)
e: Genetic modification in cows can increase milk yield and quality.

q: Transgenic animals can be used to produce pharmaceutical products by using a ____ plasmid vector. (2024-နောက်ဆက်တွဲမေးခွန်း)
e: Recombinant plasmid vectors are used to transfer desired genes into target animals for pharmaceutical production.
